acceptance_note: a few regression tests (unchanged USD pricing, 9-unit orders, general items taxed, plain parsing) pass on the untouched baseline

tasks.title: BREAKING: round money to the currency's minor unit
tasks.description:
Yen orders come out with two decimals (e.g. shipping 999.80 JPY) because round_money always rounds to cents.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tally.money.CURRENCY_DECIMALS` gains `"JPY": 0` (USD and EUR stay 2).
- `round_money(amount, currency)`: `currency` becomes a REQUIRED second positional parameter; the amount is rounded half up to that currency's decimals (`round_money(Decimal("1234.5"), "JPY") == Decimal("1235")`, exponent 0). An unknown currency raises ValueError.
- `format_money(amount, currency)` prints the currency's decimals: `"1235 JPY"`, `"3.00 USD"`.
- Every caller of round_money in tally/ passes the order's currency, so all Totals fields of a JPY order are whole yen. USD results do not change.
- tests/ updated for the new signature (tests/test_money.py calls round_money with one argument today); add tests in tests/test_currency_precision.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.
- This breaks every caller of round_money, including code other agents are writing right now in tally/pricing.py: publish a change notice (kind signature) affecting tally/money.py and tally/pricing.py when it lands.

tasks.title: Bulk discount and the SPRING15 code
tasks.description:
Wholesale customers want an automatic discount, and marketing wants a spring code.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tally.pricing.apply_discount(order, amount)`: when the order has at least 10 units in total (the sum of item quantities across all lines), add a bulk rate of 0.05 to the code's rate (no code: 0). The combined rate is capped at 0.25. The discount is `amount * rate`, rounded as today.
- `tally.rules.DISCOUNT_CODES` gains `"SPRING15": Decimal("0.15")`; codes stay case-insensitive.
- Examples: 10 units, no code, amount 100.00 -> 5.00; 10 units with WELCOME10 -> 15.00; 12 units with VIP20 -> rate 0.25.
- Unit tests in tests/test_bulk_discount.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Free shipping above a per-zone threshold
tasks.description:
Ship free when the order is large enough.

Acceptance criteria:
- New table `tally.rules.FREE_SHIPPING_OVER = {"US": Decimal("100.00"), "EU": Decimal("120.00"), "JP": Decimal("15000")}` (zone -> threshold).
- `tally.pricing.shipping_cost(order, merchandise)` returns zero (rounded like other amounts) when `merchandise` (the subtotal after discount) is greater than or equal to the zone's threshold, unless the order's total weight (sum of weight_kg * quantity) is above 30 kg. A zone without a threshold never ships free. Otherwise the fee is unchanged.
- Gift-wrap and other fees never count toward the threshold.
- Unit tests in tests/test_free_shipping.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Tax-exempt categories and new tax regions
tasks.description:
Books and food are not taxed, and we now sell to Texas and France.

Acceptance criteria:
- New `tally.rules.TAX_EXEMPT_CATEGORIES = frozenset({"books", "food"})`, matched against `Item.category`.
- `tally.pricing.tax_for(order, merchandise)`: the discount is spread over lines in proportion to their line totals, so the taxable amount is `merchandise * taxable_lines / subtotal`, where `taxable_lines` is the sum of line totals of non-exempt items and `subtotal` the order's subtotal; tax is that amount times the region's rate, rounded once at the end. A zero subtotal gives zero tax.
- `tally.rules.TAX_RATES` gains `"US-TX": Decimal("0.0625")` and `"EU-FR": Decimal("0.20")`.
- Unit tests in tests/test_tax_exempt.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Parse amounts with symbols, separators and codes
tasks.description:
The CSV importer receives amounts like "$1,234.50" that parse_money rejects.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tally.money.parse_money(text) -> Decimal` accepts, around optional whitespace: a leading `-` or surrounding parentheses for negatives (`"(12.00)"` -> -12.00); an optional leading symbol `$`, `€` or `¥`; `,` thousands separators; an optional trailing space and three-letter uppercase currency code (`"1,234 JPY"` -> 1234). The value is not rounded.
- Anything else raises ValueError (not decimal.InvalidOperation): `""`, `"abc"`, `"12.3.4"`, `"$"`, `"USD"`.
- Unit tests in tests/test_parse_money.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Gift wrapping fee
tasks.description:
Customers can ask for gift wrapping at a flat fee.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tally.models.Order` gains `gift_wrap: bool = False`.
- New table `tally.rules.GIFT_WRAP_FEE = {"USD": Decimal("5.00"), "EUR": Decimal("5.00"), "JPY": Decimal("700")}` (fee in the order's currency).
- `tally.models.Totals` gains `gift_wrap_fee: Decimal = Decimal("0")` (keep existing positional construction working).
- `tally.pricing.order_total(order)` sets `gift_wrap_fee` to the currency's fee when `order.gift_wrap`, and adds it to `total`. The fee is not discounted, not taxed, and does not count toward any free-shipping threshold.
- Unit tests in tests/test_gift_wrap.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Small-order surcharge
tasks.description:
Tiny orders lose money on handling; add a surcharge.

Acceptance criteria:
- New table `tally.rules.SMALL_ORDER_FEE = {"USD": (Decimal("20.00"), Decimal("2.50")), "EUR": (Decimal("20.00"), Decimal("2.50")), "JPY": (Decimal("2500"), Decimal("300"))}` (currency -> (threshold, fee)).
- `tally.models.Totals` gains `small_order_fee: Decimal = Decimal("0")` (keep existing positional construction working).
- `tally.pricing.order_total(order)`: when the order has at least one item and its merchandise (subtotal after discount) is strictly below the currency's threshold, set `small_order_fee` to the fee and add it to `total`. The fee is not taxed.
- Unit tests in tests/test_small_order_fee.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.

tasks.title: Customer notes on the invoice
tasks.description:
Customers leave delivery notes that the warehouse never sees.

Acceptance criteria:
- `tally.models.Order` gains `notes: str = ""`.
- `tally.invoice.render_invoice(order, number)` adds the line `Notes: <notes>` directly after the `Region:` line when the notes contain anything besides whitespace. Runs of whitespace, including newlines, become one space and the text is stripped. Without notes the invoice is unchanged.
- Unit tests in tests/test_invoice_notes.py; `python3 -m unittest` passes.
